newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares inch up at close on thirdliners.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares inch up at close on thirdliners.

text.p: Manila shares finished a shade up on Friday as strong buying was again focused on tertiary issues while activity on blue chips remained subdued, traders said.

"The market opened down but it showed resilience as it recovered despite the news of an oil price hike. There was a lot of attention on thirdliners, which were not heavy on the index," said Jose Ricardo Garcia, executive vice-president at Diversified Securities Inc.

Traders said the announcement of a 26 centavo per litre oil price increase effective Friday dampened sentiments at the open but good macroeconomics prevailed and the index immediately recovered in early trade.
Value of shares traded on Friday was average at 2.5 billion pesos. All sectors rose and gainers beat decliners 73 to 48 with 81 issues left unchanged.
Joey Roxas, president at Eagle Securities said that a mild correction may be seen early next week as punters who bought up speculative issues would likely decide to take profits.
Once 1996 company earnings results trickle in by late next week, investors are seen throwing back their money to blue chips or secondliners with stories to tell.
